southern_california.text: The marine pattern is fairly steady through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 3-12 kt; morning is favored on 7 of 7 days. Combined seas range 3.0-4.0 ft with 9-17 sec periods. Best current windows: 11-09 AM, 11-11 AM, 11-06 AM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

central_california.text: The marine pattern is improving through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 5-14 kt; morning is favored on 4 of 7 days. Combined seas range 7.0-11.0 ft with 12-16 sec periods. Best current windows: 11-11 PM, 11-10 AM, 11-12 PM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

northern_california.text: The marine pattern is deteriorating through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 3-18 kt; morning is favored on 4 of 7 days. Combined seas range 7.0-14.0 ft with 13-17 sec periods. Best current windows: 11-06 PM, 11-10 PM, 11-08 PM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

oregon.text: The marine pattern is fairly steady through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 3-29 kt; morning is favored on 5 of 7 days. Combined seas range 11.0-18.0 ft with 13-16 sec periods. Best current windows: 11-06 AM, 11-08 PM, 11-12 AM. Safety screen blocks: 11-07, 11-09, 11-10. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

washington.text: The marine pattern is improving through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 9-34 kt; morning is favored on 3 of 7 days. Combined seas range 12.0-22.0 ft with 8-15 sec periods. Safety screen blocks: 11-06, 11-07, 11-08, 11-09, 11-10, 11-11, 11-12. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The sea bass are still being caught near Davenport and 4 Mile Beach. There have been some sea bass caught between South Rock and Natural Bridges. The sea bass are near the bottom in 90-120 feet of water. There were some bluefin caught 12 miles out of Santa Cruz and Monterey. The rock fishing was better since the swell dropped. The wind was calmer today.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast November 6, 2026 Eureka, Trinidad Crab Openers Delayed Due to Domoic Acid In press release issued on Nov. 6, CDFW has taken the recommendation of the CA Dept. of Public Health to delay the Dungeness crab season from he southern boundary of the Reading Rock State Marine Protected Areas (41⁰ 17.6’ N. latitude) to the southern boundary of the Ten Mile State Marine Reserve (39° 33.3’ N. latitude). This area includes Trinidad and Eureka. CDFW Statement: State health agencies have determined that Dungeness crab from the southern boundary of the Reading Rock State Marine Protected Areas (41⁰ 17.6’ N. latitude) to Cape Mendocino, Humboldt County (40⁰ 10’ N. latitude) pose a human health risk due to elevated levels of domoic acid and recommended a delay of the recreational Dungeness crab fishery. Following this recommendation, California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) Director Meghan Hertel has delayed the recreational Dungeness crab fishery in this area. This follows action taken by Director Hertel on Oct. 30 to restrict the use of recreational crab traps due to entanglement risk and delay the opening of the fishery in southern Humboldt County/northern County d

field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: We had amazing Lingcod fishing this morning on the Tacklebuster and the Surfrider. Both vessels had over 30+ Lingcod for each boat. That is a whole bunch of the "toothy critters". The rockfish were also biting with really good scores on them as well. We have one more day of good ocean weather tomorrow and then the ocean seems to be blowing up again the start of next week. It looks like lots of swell hitting the area next week and beyond for the beginning of November. Keep in touch with our office for weather changes or trips scheduled.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
